title: Best AI Browsers in 2026: 8 Compared Feature by Feature
summary: The best AI browsers in 2026 compared feature by feature: Aside, Comet, Chrome, Safari, Edge, Opera Neon, Dia and Brave, with prices and what each can do.
body_markdown:
You want a browser that does more than summarize the page you are on. Most lists rank AI browsers by feature count, so a chat sidebar and an agent that finishes your errand end up side by side. And the best-known one is gone: ChatGPT Atlas[stopped working on August 9, 2026](https://community.openai.com/t/atlas-is-scheduled-to-stop-working-on-august-9-2026/1389473) .


Start with Aside. Give its agent the result you want and it does the clicking, typing and signing in for you, on websites and in your desktop apps. Seven other browsers, Safari included, are compared below feature by feature, with what each one charges and where each one stops.


## What is the best AI browser in 2026?#


Aside is the best AI browser in 2026 for getting tasks done. You say what you want, and its agent does the clicking and typing, on the sites you are signed in to and in your desktop apps. It comes with the free plan and runs on Mac and Windows. The other seven each miss at least one of those.


Here are the eight, from each company's own pages on November 16, 2026.


AI browsers compared: Aside, Comet, Chrome, Edge, Opera Neon, Brave, Dia and Safari by price, platforms and five agent features


## How do the AI browsers compare feature by feature?#


Six of the eight can act on websites in some form, but the terms differ: paid plans, US-only rollouts or early testing. Only Aside's agent also works in desktop apps on both Mac and Windows. Scheduled tasks, your own AI model and help with logins vary browser by browser, as the chart above shows.


## How did we rank these AI browsers?#


By one question: how much of the task does the browser finish for you? Then we read each company's own pages for the facts in the chart above: what the AI does, what it costs, where it is available and which computers it runs on. We did not run a head-to-head task test across all eight.


Aside makes one of the eight, so we kept the comparison to facts you can check. Two outside views:[9to5Mac](https://9to5mac.com/2026/07/10/with-chatgpt-atlas-shutting-down-here-are-the-ai-browsers-people-actually-use/) (Jul 10, 2026) included Aside among the browsers to use instead of ChatGPT Atlas, and[Toolfolio](https://toolfolio.com/articles/best-ai-browsers-compared-comet-dia-aside-ego-and-what-replaced-chatgpt-atlas) (Nov 2, 2026) picked "Aside for hands off agent tasks."


## Which AI browser can actually do tasks for you?#


Aside, Comet, Chrome, Edge and Opera Neon each ship an agent that clicks and types for you, and Brave is testing one. Chrome's and Edge's need a paid plan and are limited by country, and Opera Neon's needs $19.90 a month. Aside's is in the free plan on Mac and Windows and starts from your own logins.


In Aside you name the site and the result, then let it run. One example from Aside's guide to[running tasks](https://docs.aside.com/help/tasks) : "Sign in to Rippling, get my paystubs for this month, and save the PDFs to Downloads. Ask if Rippling needs MFA or a verification code."


Aside's task view after collecting the latest posts from Aside's LinkedIn page, Nov 16, 2026


[John Jeong](https://x.com/computeless/status/2069576387892281729) (Jun 23, 2026) wrote: "I can confidently say Aside is the best AI browser I've used to date. I've tried Atlas, Comet, and most of the AI browsers built by the big companies, but none of them really stuck with me."


## Can an AI browser work in your desktop apps?#


Aside can. Computer Use lets its agent open and work in the desktop apps on your Mac or Windows PC, outside the browser, and it is available on every plan. In Cua Driver Bench, a test run by Scale, Aside Computer Use ranked #1 and passed 88 of 90 trials.


[Cua Driver Bench](https://huggingface.co/spaces/earakely-scale/CuaDriverBench-AgentEnv) checks whether an AI agent can finish real office tasks across desktop apps without disturbing someone working on the same computer. With Claude Opus 5.5, Aside Computer Use scored 97.8%. Cua Driver scored 74.4%, Codex Computer Use 51.1% and agent-desktop 47.8%. Scale ran every tool through the same coding agents on macOS. None of the other seven browsers on this list was in the test.


Cua Driver Bench results by Scale


*Source:[Aside Computer Use ranks #1 in Cua Driver Bench](https://aside.com/blog/aside-computer-use-ranks-number-one-in-cua-driver-bench) (Nov 11, 2026).*


On a Mac, Aside does most of this in the background, so you can keep working while it runs. With Claude Sonnet 5.5 it passed 37 of 40 background trials without disturbing the user. On Windows it takes the screen while it acts.


The other agents stay inside the browser. Microsoft says of Browse with Copilot that "all actions run locally in your browser," and Opera says Neon Do "runs locally within your browser and directly interacts with webpages." Perplexity handles desktop apps in a separate app that controls Mac apps; its help center says "Installed-app control is not yet available on Windows."


Garry Tan, CEO of Y Combinator, which backs Aside,[posted on X](https://x.com/garrytan/status/2118951284376285508) (Nov 6, 2026): "Computer use on Aside is *amazing* and also has an added benefit of literally being a real Chromium browser that few/almost no sites can block."


Turn it on in Settings > Agents, then start a task yourself and name the app.


## Is there a free AI browser that can automate tasks?#


Yes. Aside's free plan includes the agent, with 500 credits a month, up to 3 active routines and a built-in password manager. You can also connect a ChatGPT or Claude subscription you already pay for and run the agent on that. Details are on[aside.com/pricing](https://aside.com/pricing) .


Aside also runs on a GitHub Copilot or Grok subscription, your own API key, or a local model through Ollama or LM Studio ([Configure AI providers](https://docs.aside.com/help/ai) ).


Two others have a free route with a catch. Brave's agent costs nothing while it is in early testing, and it works signed out of your sites. Opera Neon is free if you bring an outside agent of your own.


## What is the best AI browser for Mac and Windows?#


Aside runs on both: macOS 15.0 or later, and Windows 10 version 22H2 or later or Windows 11, with installers for x64 and ARM64. The agent and Computer Use work on both. That matters if you use a Windows PC at work and a Mac at home, or the other way around.


When you first open Aside it can import from browsers including Chrome, Safari, Arc and Dia, so you start with your bookmarks and history ([Get started](https://docs.aside.com/help/get-started) ).


Aside's import screen, Nov 16, 2026. It lists the browsers it finds on your computer


## What do the other seven AI browsers do, and where do they stop?#


Comet, Chrome, Edge and Opera Neon each have an agent, behind a paid plan, a US-only rollout or a separate app. Brave is testing one. Dia turns your tabs and work apps into briefs and reports. Safari summarizes pages and has no web agent yet. Each is described below from its own pages.


### Perplexity Comet#


Comet is Perplexity's browser, built on Chromium. Its Assistant sits in a side panel and answers from the tab you are on, "or any tab you mention with @." The same Assistant can click, type, fill in forms and run checkout flows.


What that costs is unclear. Perplexity's pricing table ticks Comet Assistant on the Free plan, while its help center lists "Browser Agent (Comet Assistant) Queries" as "No" on Free. Perplexity says "Comet never has access to your passwords or payment data." Where it stops: the browser itself does not work in your desktop apps.


### Chrome with Gemini#


Gemini in Chrome answers questions about the tab you are on, or up to 10 tabs you share with it. Auto browse goes further and completes multi-step tasks on websites. Google's help page says you need to be 18 or over and in the US, set your device to English, and have a paid Google AI plan.


Google's own pages differ on the details: the pricing page adds India and names only the Pro and Ultra plans, while the help page also lists the $4.99 Plus plan. For payments, Gemini "may ask you to take over the task." Where it stops: paid, limited by country and language, and not on iPhone or iPad.


### Microsoft Edge with Copilot#


Copilot in Edge summarizes pages, PDFs, videos and open tabs, free within limits. Browse with Copilot is the part that acts: it clicks, types and moves between tabs while you watch. Microsoft's Edge blog (May 13, 2026) says it is on "Edge desktop for Microsoft 365 Premium Subscribers in the U.S. only."


Microsoft says the agent "cannot access autofill data, saved passwords, or wallet information," so it works on sites where you are already signed in, and it asks before buying, booking or sending email. The same post retired Edge's earlier Copilot Mode. Where it stops: US only, paid, Windows and macOS.


### Opera Neon#


Neon has had a free plan since August 12, 2026: the browser, basic AI chat, and a built-in MCP server and command line so agents you already use can drive it. Opera calls it "the first major AI browser to offer a built-in MCP server."


Neon's own agent, Neon Do, needs the Standard plan, which also adds scheduled tasks and a choice of models. It pauses when "completing a transaction or downloading a file" needs your confirmation. Where it stops: its own agent is paid, and there is no mobile version yet.


### Brave with Leo#


Leo is Brave's built-in assistant. It is free, and Brave says "no account or signup is required." It summarizes pages and PDFs, and reading across several tabs is free too. You can run it on a local model or connect a third-party API.


Brave is testing an agent called AI browsing, which you switch on yourself on desktop. Brave keeps it in a separate profile, where "cookies, logged-in state" from your regular profile "do not cross." Where it stops: the agent is experimental and does not start signed in to your sites.


### Dia#


Dia comes from the team that made Arc. It answers from the page, your tabs and your connected apps, and builds a Morning Brief, reports and decks. Since November 12, 2026 it can also create and edit Figma files, and it "always asks before it creates anything in your Figma account."


Dia can fill in a form or draft an email once you approve the content. Its security page says its agent is "unable to navigate on its own to another website." Its pricing page calls the free plan "a better browser, without the AI." Where it stops: it does not run a multi-step task across sites.


### Safari#


Safari comes on every Mac, iPhone and iPad, and its AI is Apple Intelligence. It can summarize a page, sort your tabs with Organize by Topic, and Notify Me "can periodically check a webpage for updates, like price changes and item availability." You can also connect a ChatGPT account.


Safari has no agent that clicks through websites today. Apple announced one for passwords, where Passwords "securely navigates through websites" on your behalf, and its Apple Intelligence page marks it "Coming in a future software update." Apple Intelligence is free for now and needs a Mac with M1 or later. Where it stops: no web agent yet, and Apple devices only.


## Questions people choosing an AI browser ask#


**Can the agent see my passwords?**
No.[Aside Vault](https://docs.aside.com/help/password-manager) fills your login into the page, and the agent never receives the password itself. You choose when agents may use saved logins: always, only while the vault is unlocked, or never.


**Can I limit what the agent is allowed to do?**
Yes. Every task has a[permission mode](https://docs.aside.com/help/security) . Read only lets it look without changing your files. Guard keeps it to folders you approve and is the default. Full access lets it read and write anywhere on the computer.


**Can I run a task without my logins?**
Yes. Run it in Incognito mode. The task gets none of your normal browser profile, and agents cannot use the password manager in incognito sessions.


**Can I message the agent when I am away from my computer?**
Yes, on Pro and Max. Channels let you start and steer tasks from Slack, Telegram or Discord while Aside runs them on your computer.


See what the[browser agent](https://aside.com/features/browser-agent) can do, then download Aside for Mac or Windows at[aside.com/download](https://aside.com/download) .
